title: Equivalence-arrow spaces descend along fully faithful simplicial cocones
statement:
Let $\mathcal V$ be presentably monoidal and use [def-coef-complete-algebroid] for algebroids, fully faithful maps, essential surjectivity, universes and smallness. For a $\mathcal V$-algebroid $C$ let $U(C)$ be its object space, $I_n(C)=\operatorname{Map}(E^n,C)$ and $I(C)=|I_\bullet(C)|$, as in [lem-coef-algebroid-equivalence-nerve]. The two vertex inclusions $E^0\to E^1$ define $I_1(C)\to U(C)^2$. Let $C_\bullet:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ be a small coherent simplicial diagram whose every structure map is fully faithful and essentially surjective. Let $(j_n:C_n\to B)$ be a coherent cocone to a $\mathcal V$-algebroid $B$. Suppose every $j_n$ is fully faithful, and the induced comparison $|U(C_\bullet)|\to U(B)$ is an equivalence. Then the natural transformation $I_1(C_\bullet)\to U(C_\bullet)^2$ has pullback naturality squares, and for every $n$ its realization square
$$\begin{matrix}I_1(C_n)&\longrightarrow&|I_1(C_\bullet)|\\ \downarrow&&\downarrow\\ U(C_n)^2&\longrightarrow&|U(C_\bullet)|^2\end{matrix}$$
is a homotopy pullback. Moreover the canonical comparison
$$|I_1(C_\bullet)|\longrightarrow I_1(B)$$
is an equivalence, compatibly with the maps to $U(B)^2\simeq|U(C_\bullet)|^2$. No completeness assumption on $B$ or any $C_n$ is imposed.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, final completeness argument from the diagram over object-space squares to the two-out-of-three argument on fibers; generalized from C^{E^bullet} to a fully faithful, essentially surjective simplicial diagram and a fully faithful cocone with colimiting object spaces. Uses Proposition 5.3.6, Lemma 5.3.5 and the cited HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9. Read the retained GH.html source, arXiv:1312.3178v4. Not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this operadic infinity-category result.

proof.text: Write $X_n=U(C_n)$ and $Y_n=I_1(C_n)$, so the endpoint map is $Y_n\to X_n^2$. The definition of the algebroid nerve gives $I_0(C)\simeq U(C)$, and the equivalence-nerve lemma says that a fully faithful map induces equivalences on the fibers of $I_1$ over every pair of source objects. For a structure map $C_m\to C_n$, compare $Y_m$ with $X_m^2\times_{X_n^2}Y_n$. The comparison is an equivalence on each homotopy fiber over a point of $X_m^2$; applying the fiberwise comparison clause of geometric descent with the identity cover $X_m^2\to X_m^2$ shows that this comparison is an equivalence. Hence every naturality square of $Y_\bullet\to X_\bullet^2$ is a homotopy pullback.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, final completeness argument; Lemma 5.3.5, together with HTT Theorem 6.1.3.9

proof.text: Apply cartesian geometric descent to the transformation $Y_\bullet\to X_\bullet^2$ from Step 1. The descent lemma states that realization commutes with finite products and that a transformation whose operator squares are pullbacks has, in every degree $n$, a pullback square from $Y_n$ to $|Y_\bullet|$ over $X_n^2\to|X_\bullet|^2$. Therefore the displayed realization square in the item is a homotopy pullback for every $n$, with $|X_\bullet|^2\simeq|U(C_\bullet)|^2$.

source.place: Theorem 6.1.3.9(4), applied to the endpoint transformation

proof.text: The unique map $[0]\to[n]$ in $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ gives a structure map $C_0\to C_n$, which is fully faithful and essentially surjective by hypothesis. The equivalence-nerve criterion therefore lets every endpoint in degree $n$ be replaced, up to an object equivalence, by one from degree zero; composition with such endpoint equivalences induces equivalences of enriched mapping objects. Thus the degree-zero fiber comparison below controls all endpoint fibers and is independent of representatives.

source.place: Lemma 5.3.4 and Lemma 5.3.5, objectwise essential-surjectivity and invariance under object equivalence

proof.text: Let $q:|Y_\bullet|\to |X_\bullet|^2\times_{U(B)^2}I_1(B)$ be the pullback comparison induced by the cocone. By assumption $|X_\bullet|\to U(B)$ is an equivalence, hence so is $|X_\bullet|^2\to U(B)^2$. The square of Step 2 for $n=0$ identifies the homotopy fiber of $|Y_\bullet|$ over the image of any pair in $X_0^2$ with the corresponding fiber of $Y_0$. Since $j_0$ is fully faithful, the equivalence-nerve lemma identifies that fiber with the fiber of $I_1(B)$ over its image pair. The map $X_0^2\to|X_\bullet|^2$ is surjective on components by geometric descent and its finite-product clause. Hence $q$ is an equivalence by the fiberwise comparison criterion of geometric descent. Unwinding $q$ gives the canonical comparison $|I_1(C_\bullet)|\to I_1(B)$; its construction is the cocone map, so it is compatible with $U(B)^2\simeq|U(C_\bullet)|^2$.

source.place: Theorem 5.6.2, final fiberwise comparison and two-out-of-three argument; Proposition 5.3.6
